response: Yes, immediate old retention in [barriers.rs](file:///home/brianheineman/development/ristretto-gc-workspaces/gc-alpha-mature-numeric-barrier-probe-v1/ristretto_gc/src/collector/barriers.rs#L15-L45) is correct for existing white young targets because `!marked(1, old_epoch)` triggers `mark(1, old_epoch, Retention::Strong)` without enqueuing on the old mark queue, making `visible_retention` immediately visible to a fresh young start's `CrossRoots` while `old_handoff_unit` in [old_generation.rs](file:///home/brianheineman/development/ristretto-gc-workspaces/gc-alpha-mature-numeric-barrier-probe-v1/ristretto_gc/src/old_generation.rs#L95-L108) keys off `old_birth` (not `marked`) and still scans their old edges. It is also correct for post-snapshot black young targets because `mark_born` records `BORN_AFTER_RETIREMENT` (`marked == true` and `retention == None` in [mark_state.rs](file:///home/brianheineman/development/ristretto-gc-workspaces/gc-alpha-mature-numeric-barrier-probe-v1/ristretto_gc/src/mark_state.rs#L36-L64)), so `!marked || retention.is_some()` returns `false` and leaves old retention `None` so a fresh young start can still collect them, while `shade_live_domains` still shades any already-active young domain normally. Yes, a stopped producer can still delay phase transitions in both domains because the fallback in [barriers.rs](file:///home/brianheineman/development/ristretto-gc-workspaces/gc-alpha-mature-numeric-barrier-probe-v1/ristretto_gc/src/collector/barriers.rs#L370-L375) holds `barrier_guard()` across `shade_live_domains`, which either keeps `ACTIVE_MASK` nonzero in [publication_state.rs](file:///home/brianheineman/development/ristretto-gc-workspaces/gc-alpha-mature-numeric-barrier-probe-v1/ristretto_gc/src/publication_state.rs#L160-L242) (making `observe_phase()` return `None`) or holds a legacy `publication` read lock (making `try_publication_write()` fail) until the producer resumes and drops the guard.
